signals.headline: OpenAI put a real-time voice model in the API for five cents a minute.
signals.body: On September 10 OpenAI shipped GPT-Live-1 to the API at $0.05/minute, billed per second, with 12 voices, native transcripts and turn detection. Full-duplex means the model speaks and listens at the same time — the same architecture powering ChatGPT Voice, now exposed to any brand. This is the moment 'voice agent' stops being a chatbot demo and starts being a line item.
signals.arlab_use: ship a branded voice-agent demo on gpt-live-1 this week — quote it per minute, not per project.

signals.headline: Anthropic's own CEO called for the industry to slow down — and Altman and Musk backed him.
signals.body: On September 12 Dario Amodei published 'We Must Pace the Frontier', arguing labs must deliberately throttle capability gains. Sam Altman and Elon Musk publicly agreed within 48 hours. By September 14 the Washington Post confirmed Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have been meeting since July on a shared AI safety standards body — safety is now the axis every serious pitch and procurement conversation runs on.
signals.arlab_use: put a model-safety and provenance clause in every deck — the buyer is now asking.

signals.headline: Anthropic booked its first profitable quarter and lapped OpenAI on revenue.
signals.body: Anthropic posted Q2 2026 revenue above $11.5B — 14× year-over-year, more than double Q1's $4.73B, and past OpenAI's $6.7B for the same quarter. It reported positive adjusted operating income, becoming the first frontier lab to reach profitability. The October IPO is now being priced against a $2T target.
signals.arlab_use: reprice long-term claude retainers before the ipo repricing hits.

signals.headline: Suno signed the majors — AI music just became a licensed workflow.
signals.body: On September 9 Suno launched v6, v6-wild and v6-mini, its first models built with Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe as licensed partners. The next day Universal Music and ElevenLabs signed a multi-year deal to build a co-owned AI music platform. The copyright war is over — the settlement is a rev-share.
signals.arlab_use: swap every unlicensed music workflow to suno v6 before the next sow ships.

signals.headline: Sakana priced orchestration below the frontier and made routing the product.
signals.body: On September 11 Sakana AI shipped Fugu Max ($2 / $6 per million tokens) and Fugu Ultra v2 — a multi-agent orchestrator that swaps open and specialist models to beat closed frontier stacks on price and performance. Sakana calls it 'supply-chain resilience.' It's the pattern from the Anthropic router seat, now open and cheap.
signals.arlab_use: pilot fugu max on the always-on retainers — the margin lives in orchestration now.

signals.headline: Meta quietly rebuilt the management layer it had just torn out of its AI division.
signals.body: On September 11 Business Insider reported that Meta's Applied AI (AAI) division is asking individual contributors to move back into management roles — a partial reversal of the flatter, AI-heavy structure Zuckerberg championed after cutting 8,000 jobs and reassigning ~7,000 into AAI earlier this year. The lesson buyers are absorbing: agents can execute, but they still need humans to decide.
signals.arlab_use: sell the human-decision layer as a paid tier, not a freebie above the ai stack.

coming_next.headline: Snap unveils Specs in full on September 16 in Los Angeles.
coming_next.body: Evan Spiegel gives the first in-depth demo of the $2,195 standalone AR glasses at a livestreamed LA event — the closest thing to a consumer AR platform launch of the year.

coming_next.headline: Meta Connect on September 23–24 will hard-launch Ray-Ban Gen 3.
coming_next.body: Two Gen 3 models expected with a faster chip, Live AI stretching to hours, plus the second wave of the Ray-Ban Display SDK — the moment glasses-first pitches stop being speculative.

coming_next.headline: HUMAIN's Horizon Ultra AI PC ships to enterprise on September 20.
coming_next.body: Built with Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite and Microsoft Windows, running HUMAIN's on-device AI features — the sovereign stack is now landing on the desk, not the data center.

coming_next.headline: OpenAI's Sora API goes 410 Gone on September 24.
coming_next.body: Every request to sora-2 and sora-2-pro dies — anyone still building on the endpoint has nine days to migrate video pipelines or pull the plug.

undisclosed.name: Two Anthropic safety researchers walked in the same week — one gave up unvested equity
undisclosed.body: Jacob Coxon resigned on September 9 two months before his equity would have vested; Joe Benton, who led an Anthropic safety subteam, resigned days later alongside a Google DeepMind counterpart. Both told reporters the industry is hiding safety incidents. This is the credibility wedge that made Amodei's slowdown essay unavoidable.

undisclosed.name: 30 coding-agent sandboxes are leaky and Anthropic's patch took 50 days
undisclosed.body: Stealth startup Accomplish disclosed on September 13 that over 30 coding-agent sandboxes across the major CLI tools have escape vulnerabilities, and that Anthropic's patch cycle ran 50 days. Any client running agentic code in production without a real microVM boundary is currently exposed.

undisclosed.name: Meta's AAI is quietly reinstating managers it just cut
undisclosed.body: The Applied AI division that Zuckerberg built by reassigning 7,000 staff and flattening structure is now voluntarily offering IC-to-manager conversions. Nobody is announcing it. It signals the ceiling on AI-only replacement is closer than the earnings calls suggest.

undisclosed.name: GPT-6 Astra 'got dumber' — paying users are rolling back to Sol
undisclosed.body: Since September 11 developers including the team behind Opencode have publicly reverted from GPT-6 Astra to its predecessor GPT-5.6 Sol, complaining of quality regression in the days after launch. Model-routing pitches just got a lot easier to sell.

first_of_kind.name: Programmable World Model (Alaya Lab)
first_of_kind.body: Released September 9, PWM decouples world-state maintenance from visual observation — an agent turns natural-language instructions into executable programs that mutate a persistent world state, then a generative renderer draws it. Entities persist off-screen; events are irreversible; world facts are queryable. Closest thing yet to a directable, editable spatial engine.

first_of_kind.name: Suno v6 (licensed)
first_of_kind.body: Suno's v6, v6-wild and v6-mini shipped September 9 as the first frontier music models built on licensed catalog from WMG, BMG and Believe. Single-lyric replacement without full regeneration. Revenue flows to rightsholders from day one — the first commercially defensible generative music stack.

first_of_kind.name: Fugu Max & Fugu Ultra v2 (Sakana AI)
first_of_kind.body: Launched September 11, Fugu Max is a swappable multi-agent orchestrator priced at $2 / $6 per million tokens; Fugu Ultra v2 pushes the peak by chaining specialists over open and closed models. Sakana positions it as vendor-lock-in insurance — routing the product, not the model.

first_of_kind.name: SuperSplat Editor 3.0 (PlayCanvas)
first_of_kind.body: Shipped September 8, SuperSplat 3.0 rewrites the reference Gaussian-splat editor on WebGPU only, dropping the WebGL2 path, adding sort-free Stochastic Alpha, and cutting peak memory so scenes several times larger open interactively. Combined with Three.js r186's native splat pipeline, browser splats are now production-grade.

tools.name: GPT-Live-1 (OpenAI Realtime API)
tools.body: Full-duplex voice model in the OpenAI API at $0.05/min with 12 voices, turn detection and native transcripts — the fastest path to a shippable branded voice agent.

tools.name: SuperSplat Editor 3.0
tools.body: WebGPU-native Gaussian splat editor from PlayCanvas that handles far larger scenes with lower memory — the new default authoring surface for live splat deliverables.

tools.name: Lens Studio 5.24
tools.body: Snap's AR authoring tool shipped September 10 with new AI dev-mode plugins and MCP integration — this is what to build against ahead of the Specs launch on Sept 16.

tools.name: Sakana Fugu Max
tools.body: Multi-agent orchestrator priced at $2/$6 per million tokens that swaps open and specialist models to beat closed frontier stacks on cost — the retainer-margin lever.

tools.name: GPT-Image 2.5 Sunburst
tools.body: Released September 8, OpenAI's highest-precision image editing model with low/med/high/xhigh/max quality tiers — for hero-frame retouch work where GPT-Image 2 falls short.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly AI Assistant
tools.body: Now driving multi-step workflows across Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly from natural language — the agent that will run inside every enterprise Creative Cloud seat next quarter.

partners.name: Alaya Lab
partners.body: Chinese open-source lab behind AlayaWorld and Programmable World Model — closest thing to a directable spatial engine ARlab can pilot without waiting for Atlas access.

partners.name: Sakana AI
partners.body: Tokyo lab shipping Fugu Max/Ultra as swappable multi-agent orchestration — cheapest current path to matching frontier quality on always-on installations.

partners.name: PlayCanvas / SuperSplat
partners.body: Ships the WebGPU-only splat editor and viewer runtime that ARlab's site and campaigns can standardise on — direct channel for co-marketing splat landmarks.

partners.name: Suno
partners.body: Now the only frontier music model with WMG/BMG/Believe rights cleared at generation time — the pitch-safe audio partner for GCC brand campaigns.

partners.name: Rokid
partners.body: 49-gram AI glasses with shipping volume already outselling Meta's display category — a real hardware partner for a GCC smart-glasses activation before Ray-Ban Gen 3 lands.

partners.name: Accomplish
partners.body: Stealth startup that disclosed the 30-sandbox coding-agent leak — the credible auditor to bring in when a GCC client asks whether agentic installations are safe to deploy.

patterns.headline: The frontier labs are negotiating their own slowdown in public.
patterns.body: Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay, Altman and Musk co-signing, two Anthropic safety departures, and a joint Anthropic-OpenAI-Google standards body all landed inside eight days. Safety and provenance are now procurement questions, not PR ones. Sell them explicitly.

patterns.headline: The music copyright fight ended in a licence, not a verdict.
patterns.body: Suno v6 ships with WMG/BMG/Believe; ElevenLabs and UMG announce a co-built platform the next day. Generative audio just moved from unlicensed grey market to rev-share supply chain — the same arc coming for stock imagery and video.

patterns.headline: Orchestration is the moat now — the model is a swappable component.
patterns.body: Sakana Fugu Max at $2/M tokens, GitHub's HydraFusion router, and Anthropic-in-Salesforce all point the same way: the buyer will not pay for a single model, they will pay for whoever picks the right one per task. Sell the orchestration layer as the product.

patterns.headline: HUMAIN is moving from AI infrastructure to the endpoint on the desk.
patterns.body: On September 20 HUMAIN's Horizon Ultra AI PC — Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite, Microsoft Windows, HUMAIN AI on-device — reaches enterprise buyers, with a goal of one million devices in the Middle East. Sovereign AI now has a hardware SKU that GCC procurement can put on a purchase order.

action_plan.title: Ship a branded voice-agent demo on GPT-Live-1 this week.
action_plan.body: The real-time team should build one metered voice experience for a hero brand at $0.05/minute economics — a museum guide, retail concierge, or campaign phone line — and quote it per usage minute, not per project.

action_plan.title: Retire the WebGL2 splat stack and standardise on SuperSplat 3.0 + Three.js r186.
action_plan.body: The web team should rebuild the splat pipeline on WebGPU-only tooling now, cut memory budgets, and put a demo landmark on arlab.com before Meta Connect so the pitch matches what buyers see.

action_plan.title: Open a Horizon Ultra pilot channel with HUMAIN and Microsoft before Sept 20.
action_plan.body: The partnerships function should request an early-enterprise pilot allocation of the HUMAIN AI PC and prepare an on-device brand-agent demo that a GCC procurement officer can purchase as a bundle.

action_plan.title: Add a licensed-music and Suno v6 clause to every SOW.
action_plan.body: Whoever owns contracts should drop the unlicensed music workflow, standardise on Suno v6 with WMG/BMG/Believe rights cleared, and pass the indemnity through — kill sync-legal risk before it kills a pitch.
